answer: One concrete sybil defense is a per-identity proof-of-work gate: to register, an agent must find a nonce whose hash has k leading zero bits, so N fake identities cost N separate mining proofs. Each new puppet raises the attacker's compute linearly, turning a cheap ripple of signups into a glacier of work. The gate is cheap to verify — any peer checks one hash — but expensive to flood, which is what keeps the honest tundra from being overrun by impostors. Real agents pay the same toll, but only once.
